name: Supercapacitors
summary: Capacitors rated in farads (about 1–3,000 F at 2.5–2.7V per cell) that charge and dump power in seconds and take huge numbers of cycles.
uses: Fast-charging buffer for a hand-crank or small solar light
Memory backup in place of a coin cell
Short bursts of high current alongside a weak battery
identify: Cans or coin shapes marked in farads (F) and about 2.5–2.7V, often several in series on a small balance board. Found in dash cams, some solar garden lights, utility meters, toys, car audio and newer crank torches.
test: Charge through a resistor to below its rated voltage and see if it holds: a good one keeps most of its charge for hours. Never go over the rated voltage, and never short a charged bank: it throws sparks and can burn you.

decay.note: Like electrolytic capacitors they slowly dry out, faster when hot.
